New details on the wells that swallowed Parishan's share🔹The global registration of Gahar Lake in Lorestan under the Ramsar Convention has once again drawn attention to the status of Iran's registered wetlands.🔹Some of these wetlands have been grappling with drought for years and are still deprived of their water rights and an effective plan to restore natural conditions.🔹Parishan Wetland in Fars Province, with nearly two decades of poor conditions and hundreds of water-extraction wells, and Gavkhouni Wetland in Isfahan Province, despite the allocation of water rights and water releases into the Zayandeh Rud, are two examples of this situation.🔹Parishan Wetland has been in poor condition for about 16 to 18 years. One of the main reasons for this is the wetland's particular hydrological characteristics.🔹Parishan is one of the few wetlands in the country that does not lie at the end of a permanent river's course and has no direct river inflow. Its main source of water is rainfall and the floods that occur in the region.🔹For this reason, Parishan is more fragile than wetlands fed by permanent rivers.🔹When the groundwater table was high, rainfall would saturate the soil and raise the wetland's water level.🔹In fact, the connection between rainfall, the aquifer, and the wetland was such that water could quickly accumulate in the region and create suitable conditions for the wetland.🔹But in recent years, with increased extraction from groundwater resources, this situation has changed. There are about 490 illegal wells in the Parishan area.🖼But what plan is in place to prevent these conditions from continuing?Read here@Farsna

❇️ Head of the Reform Front of Hamadan Province: Supporting the Islamabad Agreement Requires Serious Action by the Government

🔺Ali Mehrabadi, Head of the Reform Front of Hamadan Province, speaking at a joint meeting of the Committee for Provincial Affairs of the Reform Front of Iran with the board of directors of the provincial reform fronts, held to examine ways of supporting the Islamabad Agreement, noted several positive steps taken after the agreement was signed — including the lifting of the naval blockade, the resumption of Iran's oil sales, and negotiations for the return of the country's assets — and stressed the need to clarify what has caused the agreement to stall.

▪️Stating that unless it is determined how much responsibility each party bears for derailing the agreement, and as long as leniency is shown in this regard, support campaigns will not achieve the desired outcome, he said: Supporting the agreement requires, beyond civil actions and popular campaigns, serious and responsible action by official authorities, especially the government.

▪️Ali Mehrabadi noted that despite the follow-ups, no permit has yet been issued for a gathering in support of the agreement, which the Reform Front of Iran had previously requested, and added: As long as marginal confrontations and the chanting of harsh slogans continue at nighttime gatherings, and no appropriate action is taken by official authorities — particularly the government — to manage these conditions, such campaigns in support of the agreement will yield little and will not be widely embraced by the public.

▪️In conclusion, the Head of the Reform Front of Hamadan Province, while commending the intentions of the organizers of these campaigns, expressed hope that these efforts will bear fruit, and emphasized: Alongside these actions, it is essential that Mr. Pezeshkian and the government take serious and effective measures to support those who find themselves in these difficult conditions.

Amir Mohammad Hatami, an 18-year-old from Shahin Shahr in Isfahan, was killed by a point-blank shot to his right eye after being wounded and taken into custody on the evening of 19 Dey. After 20 days of searching prisons, morgues, and security centers, his family finally identified his body—which bore signs of torture—by an old scar on his right shoulder. The 18-year-old was of Bakhtiari origin and lived in Shahin Shahr in Isfahan province. In the first days, Hatami's family had no information about their son's detention and did not know where he had been taken after being wounded. According to a source close to the family, during the search, Hatami's family would open about 100 black body bags every day in the hope of finding their son. Finally, after 20 days of searching, someone contacted the family and asked them to send a family member to identify a body. The source said: "When we went to identify Amir Mohammad, his body was inside a black bag. The blood on his body had dried and he was unrecognizable. His body and face were completely bruised." He added that Amir Mohammad's ears were severely damaged, his eyes had been gouged out, and numerous marks of injury were visible on his body. Amir Mohammad worked as a mechanic. According to those close to him, despite his young age, he was highly skilled in this trade and was known as "Osta" in Shahin Shahr. Those who knew Amir Mohammad described him as a hardworking, kind, and responsible young man who, in addition to helping provide for his family, also cared about supporting child laborers. iranintl 📡 @VahidOnline

🔺 A virtual meeting was held between members of the Committee for Provincial Affairs of the Iran Reform Front and the heads and members of the presiding boards of the provincial reform fronts, focused on examining ways for the provinces to participate in the national campaign to support the Islamabad Agreement, promoting peace-seeking, and efforts to end the war.

▪️ The guest of the meeting was Ali Shakouri-Rad, who is in charge of launching the national campaign to support the Islamabad Agreement. Outlining the goals and plans of the campaign, he described support for the agreement as a national and cross-factional endeavor and emphasized that this document was built on strong foundations—including its approval by the Supreme National Security Council, confirmation by the Leadership, and the signing of the presidents of the two countries—and should not be easily cast aside.

▪️ Pointing to the need to strengthen the voice of supporters of peace and understanding in the country's public sphere, he said: "The goal of the campaign is to create social momentum and pave the way for a more active presence of moderate forces and supporters of the agreement in the public arena—forces that, in his view, despite backing this path, have so far lacked a prominent presence and voice."

▪️ Ali Shakouri-Rad, emphasizing the importance of the Islamabad Agreement in the process of ending the war, described it as a starting point for subsequent Iran-US talks and stated that even amid disagreement and conflict, the parties cite the provisions of this agreement to advance their positions. Preserving this document and pursuing its provisions can therefore serve as a basis for continuing negotiations and reaching further understandings.

▪️ The official in charge of launching the campaign also announced meetings with foreign policy experts and the formation of specialized committees to advance the plans, stressing the need to expand this movement to the provinces. According to him, holding brainstorming sessions with experts and influential provincial figures can help clarify the dimensions of the agreement and strengthen social participation in support of peace.

▪️ The meeting continued with discussions and an exchange of views on how the provincial reform fronts can join the campaign, the holding of provincial meetings, and the mechanism for coordinating activities at the national and provincial levels.

🔹The Iran Reform Front's address on social networks: Telegram, Instagram, X (Twitter)

At some of these sites, different historical layers have formed on top of one another, becoming the earliest cores around which today's metropolises took shape. Ahvaz is one such metropolis — a city whose historical and civilizational record stretches back centuries before Islam. Despite this significance, the city's ancient heritage has been at risk of destruction over the past two decades because of metro excavations.

The project, which had been suspended since 1394 owing to financial problems and disputes between the municipality and the contractor, is now set to restart with a new contractor along the same route as before. Yet archaeologists had repeatedly warned that this area is likely linked to the ancient cities of Taryana and Hormoz Ardashir, and the artifacts discovered during metro excavation in these areas only strengthen that likelihood. But as the evidence suggests, city officials intend to resume the project without taking these warnings into account.

@mamlekate

Source: @FarsNA

Unprecedented drop in US commercial oil reserves over the past 8 months 🔹According to the latest data from the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), the country's commercial crude oil reserves fell by 8.56 million barrels in the week ending October 9, reaching approximately 415.58 million barrels.🔹This weekly decline is the largest in the past eight months and points to a significant shift in the state of US oil inventories.🔹Over the same period, US strategic crude oil reserves remained unchanged at 282.9 million barrels. The recorded decline was therefore mainly in commercial reserves, with strategic reserve inventories unchanged.🔹The data also shows that diesel and other distillate fuel reserves fell by 2.53 million barrels to 102.61 million barrels.🔹The sharp drop in commercial crude oil reserves could, if sustained, support oil prices; however, a precise assessment of its impact on the market requires examining domestic oil production, imports and exports, refinery utilization rates, and fuel demand trends in the US simultaneously.🔹The rise in gasoline reserves also shows that changes in petroleum product inventories have not been uniform, and no definitive conclusion about the overall state of demand can be drawn solely from the decline in crude oil reserves.@Farsna - Link

🔹On 30 Shahrivar, Bloomberg reported that Iran had granted permission for a Qatari LNG cargo bound for Pakistan to pass through the Iranian route in the Strait of Hormuz; that same month, another cargo had traveled from Qatar to Pakistan under the same conditions.
🔹In mid-Mehr, the maritime tracking account ManchoOSINT also reported that a third Qatari cargo had entered the Strait of Hormuz and was using the Iranian corridor en route to Pakistan.
🔹Now Bloomberg says Qatar can boost its cargo volumes through ship-to-ship transfers, but security risks cap the potential for increased exports.
🔹If the risks of transiting the Strait of Hormuz persist until early 2029, global liquefied natural gas exports may remain below pre-war-with-Iran levels until late 2027 or even late 2028.

In the Name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful

📌The auspicious birth of Hazrat Zainab Kubra (peace be upon her) — the epitome of patience and perseverance and the standard-bearer of loyalty in the most difficult arenas of divine trial — is a reminder of human glory that kept the lamp of hope alight amid suffering and affliction, and with faith and courage, etched an enduring epic of sacrifice and responsibility.

entry.title:
[Kayhan_online] 🔰Second Anniversary of Yahya Sinwar's Martyrdom
🔸October 16, 2026, marks…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @Kayhan_online

🔰Second Anniversary of Yahya Sinwar's Martyrdom

🔸October 16, 2026, marks the second anniversary of the martyrdom of Yahya Sinwar, known as "Abu Ibrahim," former head of the political bureau of the Hamas movement — a figure whose life was intertwined with captivity and the political and military developments of Gaza.

🔸Sinwar was born in 1962 in the Khan Younis camp, into a family displaced from the city of Al-Majdal. The experience of living in the camp and the aftermath of the Nakba formed the social context for the shaping of his political outlook. He studied Arabic language at the Islamic University of Gaza and expanded his political activity in the student environment — a path that was accompanied by repeated arrests at the hands of the occupation forces.

🔸His longest period of captivity began in 1988 and continued until his release in 2011. In prison, Sinwar became one of the organizational officials of Hamas prisoners, learned Hebrew, and followed developments in the society and politics of the Zionist regime. His release in the "Wafa al-Ahrar" agreement, which led to the release of 1,027 Palestinian prisoners in exchange for the Israeli soldier "Gilad Shalit," brought the issue of prisoners more prominently into his political life.

🔸In 2017, he assumed the leadership of Hamas in the Gaza Strip and was elected for another term in 2021. After the assassination of the martyr Ismail Haniyeh in Tehran, Hamas announced on August 6, 2024, the election of Sinwar as head of the movement's political bureau — an election in the midst of war that entrusted the responsibility of political leadership of the movement to the leadership based in Gaza.

🔸Sinwar was martyred on October 16, 2024, during a clash with the forces of the occupation army in Tel al-Sultan, Rafah. The army of the Zionist regime announced his martyrdom the following day, and Hamas confirmed his martyrdom on October 18. According to published reports, the forces involved were initially unaware of his identity, and identification was carried out after the clash.

🔸Images of the final moments of the martyr Sinwar in a destroyed building in Tel al-Sultan became one of the most enduring scenes of the Gaza war — images that showed him wounded and throwing a piece of wood toward an Israeli drone.

🔘 Yes | Eitaa | Soroush+ | Instagram | Telegram
@Kayhan_Online

📢 Twelve water and electricity projects inaugurated in East Azerbaijan with a budget of 124,500 billion tomans

◀️ In the presence of Mohammad Jafar Qaempanah, Executive Deputy to the President, during a visit to East Azerbaijan province today, 23 Mehr, 12 projects — including 2 water and wastewater projects and 10 electricity infrastructure projects — with a total announced budget of 124,500 billion tomans were inaugurated.

◀️ Among the inaugurated projects are a water supply project serving 150 villages in the province with a budget of 665 billion tomans, and the Azarshahr wastewater treatment plant with its transmission and collection network, Module One, with a budget of 1,740 billion tomans, both implemented by the East Azerbaijan Water and Wastewater Company.

◀️ The water supply project for 150 villages includes drilling and equipping 25 wells, building 19 reservoirs, laying 165 kilometers of transmission lines and 137 kilometers of water distribution network, rehabilitating 12 kilometers of transmission line, and constructing 6 pumping stations. With this project coming online, a stable water supply will be provided for 150 villages comprising 10,427 households and a population of over 36,745.

◀️ The Azarshahr wastewater treatment plant, using the advanced SBR method with a daily treatment capacity of 8,100 cubic meters, will serve a population of over 84,000.

◀️ Additionally, 10 electricity infrastructure projects under the responsibility of the East Azerbaijan Regional Electricity Company have been inaugurated. These projects include a 230-kilovolt double-circuit cable line to supply the central GIS substation of Tabriz via the energy tunnel, the 230-kilovolt section of the central GIS substation of Tabriz, and eight line and substation projects.

◀️ The total expenditure for the electricity projects is announced at 11,095 billion tomans, and their implementation has created jobs for 400 people. The goals of these projects include increasing the reliability of electricity supply to central Tabriz and its subordinate counties, and meeting the electricity needs of industrial parks.

entry.title: [VahidOnline] Varisha Moradi's lawyers announced on Wednesday, 22 Mehr, that Branch 15 of the…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @VahidOnline

Varisha Moradi's lawyers announced on Wednesday, 22 Mehr, that Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court — which had previously sentenced this political prisoner held in Evin to execution on charges of "membership in a rebel group" — insisted on its previous death sentence despite the Supreme Court's request to examine "deficiencies in the investigation."

Amir Sajjadi and Keyvan Azizi, Varisha Moradi's lawyers, speaking to "Emtedad," confirmed this news and stated that on Wednesday, 22 Mehr, they visited Branch 15 of the Revolutionary Court and received the verdict issued by this branch, and according to the notified verdict, they have 20 days to appeal to the Supreme Court.

According to them, this verdict was issued in a situation where the previous verdict of Branch 15 sentencing Varisha Moradi to death had been overturned by the reviewing branch in the Supreme Court after serious doubts were raised about the investigation; yet the aforementioned branch, without conducting the investigation requested by the Supreme Court, merely changed the title of the charge and once again sentenced Ms. Moradi to execution on the charge of membership in a rebel group.

Amir Sajjadi, stating that "in the lawyers' view, there are no sufficient and solid grounds for attributing such a charge to Varisha Moradi," emphasized: "Ms. Moradi has absolutely not been involved in any operations against the Islamic Republic, and her activities were solely related to her fight against ISIS in northern Syria."

Keyvan Azizi also, emphasizing that Varisha Moradi's lawyers will appeal within the legal deadline, expressed hope that "the Supreme Court, as in the previous instance, will give sufficient attention to the defenses and objections."

Varisha Moradi, who is currently imprisoned in Evin Prison, was arrested on 10 Mordad 1402 on the outskirts of Sanandaj, and on 5 Dey of the same year, upon completion of the interrogation stages, was transferred from the Ministry of Intelligence detention center known as Ward 209 of Evin Prison to the women's ward of this prison.

She was sentenced to execution on 20 Aban 1403 by Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court on charges of "baghy" (armed uprising against the government). In an open letter from prison, she revealed that during her detention she was subjected to physical and psychological torture, death threats, and gender-based violence.

@VahidHeadline📡 @VahidOnline

The clock of Hormuz was set against the enemy
🔹In a siege, time is a scarce commodity — because the enemy has targeted your resilience, not merely your soil or your fleet.
🔹Every day of delay deepens the attrition. So the besieged actor must not manage time; it must turn time into a weapon.
🔹The lesson of history is that in asymmetric balances, victory takes shape in the opponent's mind before the battlefield.
🔸Now the enemy must be brought to understand that no scenario — neither maximum pressure nor limited operations — leads to victory. This is the premise of sustainable peace.
🔹The shift in the pattern of tension in the Strait of Hormuz must now be read within this same framework. Striking a ship's propulsion, dealing firmly with Emirati vessels, punishing ships that turn off AIS — these are not merely tactics; they are messages.
🔹The Strait of Hormuz now plays the role of a clock. Every action must make the cost of passage outweigh the profit of victory and drown the opponent's will in the calculation of defeat.
🔹The main danger, however, is the pulse of negotiation at a moment when the perception of non-victory has not yet taken hold in the enemy.
🔹A signal of dialogue under these conditions is no free lunch, and it can muddy the message of power and hand time back to the opponent's favor.
🔹In a siege, trial and error is a luxury. Iran must compress time, not sell it off through hesitation. Peace comes when the opponent comes to believe that victory is impossible.

entry.title: [VahidOnline] Shahrzad Shahbazi, one of the lawyers for the defendants in the "Aliakhani…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @VahidOnline

Shahrzad Shahbazi, one of the lawyers for the defendants in the "Aliakhani Square of Isfahan" case and the lawyer for Alireza Sepahi, has rejected the narrative put forward by state media, announcing that the charge of killing law enforcement officers was never communicated to any of the defendants in this case, nor did the court address this charge. So far, five of the defendants in this case have been executed, and seven others remain at risk of execution. The lawyer's statements came in response to the publication of an interview in state media in which a woman, introduced as the wife of one of the killed officers, accuses the defendants of killing and burning officers. The interview was published after criticism mounted over the carrying out of executions, particularly the execution of Alireza Sepahi. Shahbazi also questioned the presence of this woman at the site of the executions, asking: when the case did not involve qisas or a personal right, on what basis was she allowed to be present at the site where the sentence was carried out? In a message posted on Instagram on Saturday, 18 Mehr 1405, Shahbazi wrote: "The charge of killing has under no circumstances been communicated to any of the defendants in the Aliakhani Square and Shohada Square case." She emphasized that the allegation of "burning officers in connection with premeditated murder" was neither addressed in court nor included among the charges in the verdict. Shahbazi cited the Revolutionary Court's lack of jurisdiction over this charge as the reason it did not take up the matter of killing. The Aliakhani Square case was opened after four Special Unit officers were killed during the protests of 18 Dey 1404 in Isfahan. State media had previously published videos of the defendants' confessions during interrogations, crime scene reconstructions, and trial sessions in Branch One of the Isfahan Revolutionary Court — confessions that human rights bodies consider forced and invalid. Alireza Sepahi was executed in the early hours of Monday, 13 Mehr. Mai Sato, the United Nations Special Rapporteur on human rights in Iran, in reaction to the execution, had reported serious concerns about the torture of defendants and the lack of a fair trial in this case. According to Sato, the sentence was carried out while Sepahi's lawyer was still working to have the case reviewed. Sepahi had previously also been on the verge of public execution, but was transferred to the hospital after a heart attack. That same night, citizens stayed in Aliakhani Square until dawn to prevent the executions from being carried out.@VahidHeadline📡 @VahidOnline

🔸"Trump needs an agreement" — this phrase is part of Hossein Marashi's analysis and viewpoint, which coincided with the announcement of an agreement between "Trump" and "Putin"; an agreement that, hours after being reported in the media, was trampled underfoot like the "Islamabad Agreement" by Ukraine's attack on a Russian oil refinery.

🔸Hossein Marashi said in an interview with "Khabar Online": "Trump now needs an agreement; an agreement that might help him in the elections."

🔸Simultaneously with Marashi's call for negotiations and a new agreement, "Donald Trump" and "Vladimir Putin" reached a joint solution regarding the supply of diesel fuel, which Ukraine, disregarding the agreement that had been reached, targeted the storage tanks of the "Novoshakhtinsk" oil refinery in Russia's "Rostov" region.

🔸Ukraine's attack on Russian oil facilities after the Trump-Putin agreement was reminiscent of the Zionist regime's violation of commitments after the Islamabad Agreement; violations that were met with a theatrical reaction from Trump.

🔸Trump's theatrical reaction to the violation of commitments by "Netanyahu" in the Islamabad Agreement and "Zelensky's" stonewalling in the path of implementing the Russia-America agreement is more akin to a "mock war" than a sign of seriously pursuing commitments, and is a pattern used to maintain political credibility and placate public opinion.

🔸As an example, on 24 Khordad 1405, simultaneously with the verbal agreement between Iran and America, Israel attacked Beirut, and Trump wrote in reaction to the violation of the pact: "The attack on Beirut should not have happened, especially on the special day when we are very close to a peace agreement with Iran... there should no longer be any attacks by Israel anywhere in Lebanon"; a theatrical and hollow reaction that justifies the lack of enforceability.

🔸Furthermore, with minimal positions, it prevents the restoration of lost trust and blocks the path to forming an effective mechanism to compensate for distrust.

🔸Based on history, Washington is either accused of violating commitments or, in the face of its allies' violation of pacts, contents itself with theatrical positions; in a situation where trust is the "Achilles' heel" of any agreement with America, why should we base our decision-making on Trump's need for an agreement and consent to an agreement that is subject to violation from the very beginning?!

Central Bank's final blow to the phantom deposits of trust companies

What is phantom depositing?

🔹Phantom depositing by trust companies referred to a phenomenon where the deposit of export earnings was reported to the bank, but upon attempting to use the funds, it turned out that no financial transfer had actually taken place.

🔹Last winter, the scale of phantom depositing by trust companies reached such levels that the government faced a dollar shortage. This shortage is considered one of the factors behind the government's decision to eliminate the preferential exchange rate.

What is the Central Bank's new mechanism?

🔹Under the Central Bank's new framework, trust companies must first transfer a specified amount, and only after full verification by the Central Bank do they receive authorization to move larger sums.
